object_description: a ground-floor gym, four-story school bar, and pentagonal extension
design_condition: The buildings form an ensemble around the sports field, address the street with a widened school volume, and preserve a forested river edge, although the occupied site leaves little room for future development.

positive.statement: The differentiated situation proposal integrates the large-scale buildings and the neighborhood context appropriately.
The gym roof creates an appropriate scale toward the sports field and references the town hall architecture.
The sports field with its street-side grandstand acts as a unifying outdoor element.
The organization of the gym is well thought out, with versatile use and naturally lit access spaces.
The proposed school structure promises flexible and therefore sustainable use.
The location of the new buildings integrates the town hall and the existing small building into an ensemble with connections beyond the perimeter.
The project is economically viable overall.

negative.statement: Geometric requirements and topographical conditions do not allow the proposed ground-floor gym and external ramp solution.
Public use of the outdoor spaces is possible only to a limited extent because they are mostly reserved for school operations.
The outsourced auditorium is less suitable for day-to-day school operations because it is decoupled from the school.
The planned expansion would impair school operations and must be taken into account.
Locating all parking spaces in the basement is disadvantageous for sustainability and construction costs.
The entire area is occupied, leaving little scope for development.
The classrooms are divided into four parts, losing the spatial proximity and diversity expected of a sustainable school.
